neighbours.label: the generic head of a singling-out phrase, where a superlative or 'the one that matters' is coming: 'the ⟦one⟧ I reach for most', 'the ⟦thing⟧ that matters', 'the guy ⟦who⟧…', 'the ⟦way⟧ we…', 'a ⟦good⟧ starting point'. Output promotes ' most', ' best', ' biggest', ' key'
fire: Of all the teachers at that school, the one I remember best is Mrs Okafor.
When you buy a tent, the thing that matters most is how it handles wind.
Among her many paintings, the one that draws the biggest crowds is a small portrait.
In a kitchen this small, the tool you will use most is a sharp paring knife.
Of the three proposals, the one that makes the most sense is the cheapest.
For new runners, the thing people get wrong most often is their pace.
Out of everyone on the team, the person who works hardest is the goalkeeper.
Looking back on the trip, the part I enjoyed most was the ferry crossing.
quiet: Mrs Okafor taught history at that school and retired to Devon in June.
When you buy a tent, check the seams and ask how it handles wind.
Her small portrait hangs in the east wing and draws crowds every weekend.
In a kitchen this small, a sharp paring knife hangs beside the stove.
Three proposals arrived on Monday, and the committee read them on Tuesday.
New runners often start too fast and then struggle with their pace.
Our goalkeeper trains every morning and works with the youth team at weekends.
On the trip we took a ferry crossing and then drove north for two days.

notes: Probes: 'the one I reach for most' 0.77, 'the one who stood out' 0.43, 'the thing that matters most' 0.41, but the construction fires without a superlative too ('The player who arrived late' 0.24, 'A good place to start' 0.32, 'The way to the station' 0.31), so the label is the singling-out head, not the superlative. Plain subjects 0.01-0.14.
